record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Give a simple proof, if the statement is true, that the differential system ẋ = y, ẏ = −x³ + dx²y + y³ has a unique limit cycle.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. (ii) Give a simple proof, if it is true, of the uniqueness of the limit cycle for equation { ˙x =y, ˙y =−x3 +dx2y +y3.

artifact.category_tag: limit cycles of planar polynomial systems
artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the planar polynomial differential system in $\mathbb{R}^2$ depending on a real parameter $d$:\n$$\dot{x} = y, \qquad \dot{y} = -x^{3} + d\, x^{2} y + y^{3}.$$\nA limit cycle is an isolated periodic orbit of the system. Determine whether, for every value of the parameter $d$ for which the system admits at least one limit cycle, this limit cycle is unique, and provide a simple proof of the uniqueness when it holds.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a published simple proof of uniqueness of the limit cycle for the cubic system ẋ = y, ẏ = −x³ + dx²y + y³. Related work treats uniqueness for generalized Liénard or cubic systems with different structure, but none directly addresses this particular family. The status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: On the Uniqueness of Limit Cycles in a Generalized Liénard System
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for existence, uniqueness and hyperbolicity of limit cycles in generalized Liénard systems.
status_evidence.claim: General uniqueness criteria exist for related Liénard-type systems but do not directly cover the cubic system in question.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Limit Cycle of Degree 2 for Linear Type Center Plus Cubic Homogeneous Polynomial Differential Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies linear type center plus cubic homogeneous polynomial systems and uniqueness via invariant algebraic curves.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related cubic homogeneous perturbations of linear centers are actively studied, but the specific family ẋ=y, ẏ=−x³+dx²y+y³ is not addressed.
